documents.title: A Consolidated Schema for Mathematical Knowledge: Toward a Metaontology of Mathematical Practice

social.program: a mechanism-first metaontology of mathematical practice
norms: hybrid systems that bolt a computer algebra system to a proof assistant are treated as evidence of ontological mismatch, not of bad engineering
folklore: mathematics is a single edifice of true statements connected by proof
blind_spots: the pre-formal layer has historically been treated as unworthy of formal attention

affordances: tools that can converse with, capture and manipulate pre-formal material
constraints: maintaining coherence across ontologies has a computational and conceptual cost that must be budgeted explicitly

nodes.name: Design the Schema Underneath Mathematical Practice
nodes.statement: The research direction pursued here is to design the metaontology beneath proof, symbolic manipulation and numerical experiment rather than to work inside any one of them.

shape.descriptor: go one level below the formal regimes and name the substrate they share

representation.content: This paper's goal is to design the schema underneath these three practices.

sources.heading: 1. Introduction: Mathematics Is Not One Ontology
sources.quote: This paper's goal is to design the schema underneath these three practices: the metaontology that makes their differing commitments explicit

nodes.name: The Pre-Formal Layer Has Never Been Written Down
nodes.statement: The improvisational, analogical and exploratory activity that precedes formalization has never been given a formal ontological treatment.

shape.descriptor: the layer everyone works in and nobody records

representation.content: Beneath these formal regimes lies a layer of practice that has never been formally written down.

sources.heading: Abstract
sources.quote: Beneath these formal regimes lies a layer of practice that has never been formally written down

nodes.name: Inspiration Is Individual Meta-Deductive Steering, the Social Layer Collective
nodes.statement: The inspiration layer and the social layer perform the same analogical, trajectory-shaping reasoning on the same raw materials, one internally to a mind and one externally across a community.

shape.descriptor: same steering machinery, one head versus many heads

similar_to.note: both pair an internal mechanism with its collective analog

sources.heading: 7. The Duality That Completes the Schema
sources.quote: Inspiration is individual meta-deductive steering... The social layer is collective meta-deductive steering

nodes.name: Numeric Stability Is Internal, Ecological Stability External
nodes.statement: The numeric layer and the ecological layer both operate on noise, cost, feasibility and robustness, the first mathematically and the second environmentally.

shape.descriptor: robustness under refinement versus robustness under the world

sources.heading: 7. The Duality That Completes the Schema
sources.quote: Both operate on the same raw materials — noise, cost, feasibility, robustness — one mathematically, one environmentally.

nodes.name: Duality Table Between Cognitive Layers and Their Contextual Analogs
nodes.statement: Each of the five cognitive layers is mapped to a social analog and an ecological analog, giving the schema three axes rather than a linear stack.

shape.descriptor: one dictionary row per cognitive layer

representation.content: -2 Inspiration | collective inspiration | problem ecology; 0 Fuzzy | community heuristics | environmental heuristics; 1 Symbolic | canonical formalisms | tool-driven representations; 2 Deductive | proof norms | physical/logical constraints; 3 Numeric | empirical norms | real-world stability

sources.heading: 7. The Duality That Completes the Schema
sources.quote: This gives the following duality table, which should be read as the organizing summary of the entire schema

nodes.name: Every Fuzzy Pattern Descends Through Symbolic, Deductive and Numeric Form
nodes.statement: A fuzzy pattern is expected to propagate downward into a symbolic rule, a deductive justification and a numeric consequence, and this descent pattern is claimed to recur across unrelated mathematical ideas.

sources.heading: 3.2 Worked Example: Completing the Square
sources.quote: Symmetry arguments, dimensional analysis, duality, change of basis, and perturbation expansions all follow the identical descent pattern

nodes.name: Three Different Sciences Wearing the Same Clothing
nodes.statement: Proving, symbolic manipulation and numerical experiment behave like three different sciences that merely share the vocabulary of mathematics.

representation.content: three activities that behave like different sciences wearing the same clothing

sources.heading: 1. Introduction: Mathematics Is Not One Ontology
sources.quote: three activities that behave like different sciences wearing the same clothing

nodes.name: Quadratics Simplify When a Perfect Square Is Isolated
nodes.statement: Before any formalization, completing the square exists as the unformalized pattern that quadratics become simpler if a perfect square is isolated.

shape.descriptor: isolate a perfect square and the rest goes quiet

similar_to.note: both are worked examples of the same descent pattern

representation.content: quadratics become simpler if you isolate a perfect square

sources.heading: 3.2 Worked Example: Completing the Square
sources.quote: At the fuzzy layer it exists as an unformalized pattern: quadratics become simpler if you isolate a perfect square.

nodes.name: The Laws Should Not Depend on the Observer's Frame
nodes.statement: The principle of relativity begins as the fuzzy hunch that physical laws should not depend on the observer's frame.

shape.descriptor: the description may move, the law may not

representation.content: the laws shouldn't depend on the observer's frame

sources.heading: 3.2 Worked Example: Completing the Square
sources.quote: the fuzzy hunch that "the laws shouldn't depend on the observer's frame"

nodes.name: The Six Cross-Ontology Morphisms Are the Missing Architecture
nodes.statement: No existing mathematical software implements all six cross-ontology morphisms as first-class composable operations, and their absence is the actual missing architecture of the field's tooling.

representation.content: most systems implement one or two of them ad hoc, and none implement all six as first-class, composable operations

sources.heading: 2.5 A Unifying Object and Morphism Layer
sources.quote: These six morphisms are the actual missing architecture of mathematical software today

nodes.notes: Asserted without evidence in the notes; kept fuzzy per the hedging rule.

nodes.name: What Is the Geometry of Inspiration and Fuzzy Space?
nodes.statement: It is unresolved how to make explicit the notion of similarity or distance between hunches and analogies so that tools can cluster, retrieve and extend proto-mathematical material.

sources.heading: 9. Implications and Directions for Further Work
sources.quote: making this geometry explicit would allow automated tools to cluster, retrieve, and extend proto-mathematical material in a principled way

nodes.name: Inspiration Layer (Ontology −2)
nodes.statement: The inspiration layer is defined as the stratum whose objects are directional inferences about the space of possible theories: research trajectories, domain mappings, suspected dualities, invariance hypotheses and identified gaps.

representation.content: an inspiration-layer object is not a mathematical object at all — it is a directional inference about the space of possible theories

sources.heading: 4. The Inspiration Layer: A Deductive Meta-Navigator
sources.quote: an inspiration-layer object is not a mathematical object at all — it is a directional inference about the space of possible theories

nodes.name: Fuzzy Layer (Ontology 0)
nodes.statement: The fuzzy layer is defined as the pre-formal, pre-truth-apt stratum whose objects are patterns, conjectures, sketches, metaphors and partial operators, which exist once they can be expressed at all and whose equality is similarity of conceptual shape.

representation.content: Existence: it exists once it can be expressed at all; Truth: not applicable; Equality: similarity of conceptual shape

sources.heading: 3. The Fuzzy Layer: A Fourth, Pre-Formal Ontology
sources.quote: We name this Ontology 0: the fuzzy layer, and give it the same structural treatment as the three formal ontologies.

nodes.name: Social Layer (Ontology +S)
nodes.statement: The social layer is defined as the distributed epistemic environment — citations, folklore, shared heuristics, norms, prestige gradients and funding incentives — that modulates every cognitive layer.

representation.content: references, related work, citations, prior art, folklore, shared heuristics, established metaphors, domain conventions, research programs, open-problem lists, collective blind spots, prestige gradients, funding incentives, publication norms

sources.heading: 5. The Social Layer
sources.quote: We call this Ontology +S: the social layer, and treat it as orthogonal to the cognitive stack

nodes.name: Ecological Layer (Ontology +E)
nodes.statement: The ecological layer is defined as the distributed physical and technological environment — physical constraints, engineering demands, computational limits, economic incentives and available substrates — that modulates every cognitive layer through constraint.

representation.content: physical constraints, engineering demands, computational limits, economic incentives, technological affordances, available materials and substrates

sources.heading: 6. The Ecological Layer
sources.quote: the ecological layer is the distributed physical and technological environment of the world

nodes.name: Object as Ontology Tag, Representation and Interfaces
nodes.statement: Every mathematical object is represented as a triple of an ontology tag, an ontology-specific representation and a set of cross-ontology interfaces.
nodes.formal: Object := { Ontology: {Proof, Symbolic, Numeric}, Representation, Interfaces }

representation.content: Object := { Ontology, Representation, Interfaces }

sources.heading: 2.5 A Unifying Object and Morphism Layer
sources.quote: Every mathematical object is represented as a triple of an ontology tag, an ontology-specific representation, and a set of cross-ontology interfaces

nodes.name: Completing the Square as a Rewrite Rule
nodes.statement: At the symbolic layer, completing the square is the oriented rewrite of a quadratic into a shifted perfect square plus a constant.
nodes.formal: a x^2 + b x + c \;\to\; a\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 - \frac{b^2}{4a} + c

representation.content: a x^2 + b x + c → a (x + b/2a)^2 − b^2/4a + c

sources.heading: 3.2 Worked Example: Completing the Square
sources.quote: a x^2 + b x + c → a (x + b/2a)^2 − b^2/4a + c

nodes.name: Covariance Under a Galilean Frame Change
nodes.statement: Symbolically, the relativity hunch becomes the requirement that the laws be covariant under the substitution x' = x − vt.

representation.content: covariance requirement under x' = x − vt

sources.heading: 3.2 Worked Example: Completing the Square
sources.quote: becomes, symbolically, a covariance requirement under x' = x − vt

nodes.name: Unified Workspace Engine
nodes.statement: The proposed workspace engine is a system that represents objects across all five cognitive layers uniformly, supports the morphisms between them and tracks social and ecological context as first-class metadata.

representation.content: a system — a "workspace engine" — that represents objects across all five cognitive layers uniformly

interfaces.note: no implementation or measurement exists in the notes

sources.heading: 9. Implications and Directions for Further Work
sources.quote: The ultimate practical goal of this schema is a system — a "workspace engine"

nodes.layer_rationale: The notes present this construction only as the numeric realization of completing the square — a stable method judged by robustness under refinement, not as a symbolic term.
nodes.name: Stable Method for Locating Roots and Vertex Coordinates
nodes.statement: At the numeric layer, completing the square becomes an algorithm that stably locates the roots or vertex coordinates of a quadratic.

representation.content: a stable method for locating roots or vertex coordinates

sources.heading: 3.2 Worked Example: Completing the Square
sources.quote: At the numeric layer, it becomes an algorithm: a stable method for locating roots or vertex coordinates.

nodes.name: Symbolic Ontology Commitments
nodes.statement: In the symbolic ontology a mathematical object is a term in a rewrite system, existence is well-formedness, truth is reachability of a normal form and equality is convertibility.

representation.content: Existence: well-formed syntactic construct; Truth: reachability of a normal form; Equality: convertibility

sources.heading: 2.2 The Symbolic Ontology (Rewrite-Objects)
sources.quote: Equality means convertibility — the existence of a rewrite path between two terms.

nodes.name: Deductive Ontology Commitments
nodes.statement: In the deductive ontology a mathematical object is a node in a derivation graph, existence is derivability from axioms, truth is closure under inference rules and equality is provable equivalence.

representation.content: Existence: derivability from axioms; Truth: closure under inference rules; Equality: provable equivalence

interfaces.note: extract the term from a proof

references.text: type theories such as those underlying Coq or Lean

sources.heading: 2.1 The Deductive Ontology (Proof-Objects)
sources.quote: Existence means derivability from axioms. Truth means closure under inference rules. Equality means provable equivalence.

nodes.name: Numeric Ontology Commitments
nodes.statement: In the numeric ontology a mathematical object is a limit of computable approximations, existence is convergence under some metric, truth is stability under refinement and equality is indistinguishability within an error bound.

representation.content: Existence: convergence under some metric; Truth: stability under refinement; Equality: indistinguishability within an error bound

sources.heading: 2.3 The Numeric (Analytic) Ontology
sources.quote: Equality means indistinguishability within an error bound.

nodes.name: The Consolidated Schema of Mathematical Practice
nodes.statement: Mathematical practice is described by five cognitive layers — inspiration, fuzzy, symbolic, deductive, numeric — wired together by object, morphism and coherence structures, plus two orthogonal contextual layers, social and ecological, that are the structural duals of the inspiration and numeric layers.

representation.content: five cognitive layers and two contextual layers, with an object layer, a morphism layer and a coherence layer

sources.heading: 8. The Consolidated Schema
sources.quote: the consolidated schema consists of five cognitive layers and two contextual layers

nodes.name: Physical Laws Are Lorentz-Invariant
nodes.statement: Deductively, the relativity hunch becomes the formal statement that physical laws are Lorentz-invariant.

representation.content: physical laws are Lorentz-invariant

sources.heading: 3.2 Worked Example: Completing the Square
sources.quote: deductively, the formal statement that physical laws are Lorentz-invariant

nodes.notes: Cited as a known result rather than proved in the notes.

nodes.name: Derivation That Completing the Square Preserves Equality
nodes.statement: At the deductive layer, completing the square is a proof object: a derivation showing that the rewrite preserves equality.

representation.content: a derivation showing that the rewrite preserves equality

sources.heading: 3.2 Worked Example: Completing the Square
sources.quote: At the deductive layer, it becomes a proof object — a derivation showing that the rewrite preserves equality.

nodes.name: Existence Proofs Constructed From Computation
nodes.statement: A computation can be turned into an existence proof, as when interval-arithmetic certificates discharge a claim in the deductive ontology.

representation.content: Numeric → Proof (construct existence proofs from computation, e.g. interval-arithmetic certificates)

sources.heading: 2.5 A Unifying Object and Morphism Layer
sources.quote: Numeric → Proof (construct existence proofs from computation, e.g. interval-arithmetic certificates)

nodes.name: Interval-Arithmetic Certificate
nodes.statement: An interval-arithmetic computation is offered as the paradigm case of numeric evidence that certifies a deductive existence claim.

representation.content: interval-arithmetic certificates

interfaces.note: named but never performed in the notes

sources.heading: 2.5 A Unifying Object and Morphism Layer
sources.quote: e.g. interval-arithmetic certificates

nodes.name: Stable Integrators Must Preserve the Associated Invariants
nodes.statement: Numerically, the relativity hunch becomes the requirement that stable integrators preserve the associated invariants such as energy and momentum.

representation.content: stable integrators preserve the associated invariants (energy, momentum)

sources.heading: 3.2 Worked Example: Completing the Square
sources.quote: numerically, the requirement that stable integrators preserve the associated invariants (energy, momentum)

nodes.name: The Community Decides What Counts as a Legitimate Proof
nodes.statement: The social layer shapes the deductive layer by determining what counts as a legitimate proof and which axioms are acceptable.

sources.heading: 5. The Social Layer
sources.quote: It shapes the deductive layer by determining what counts as a legitimate proof and which axioms are acceptable.

nodes.name: Mathematics Is a Single Edifice Connected by Proof
nodes.statement: It is commonly held that mathematics is a single body of true statements connected by proof, a picture the notes call useful for pedagogy but false as a description of practice.

sources.heading: 1. Introduction: Mathematics Is Not One Ontology
sources.quote: This picture is useful for pedagogy but false as a description of practice.

nodes.name: Type Systems, Morphism Catalogues and a Workspace Engine
nodes.statement: The stated agenda is to give each layer an explicit type discipline, enumerate the morphisms with operational semantics, make the geometry of inspiration and fuzzy space explicit, and build a unified workspace engine.

sources.heading: 9. Implications and Directions for Further Work
sources.quote: several directions of further work follow naturally from it

nodes.name: Type Theories Underlying Coq and Lean
nodes.statement: The notes cite the type theories underlying Coq and Lean as hosts of the deductive ontology.

references.text: type theories such as those underlying Coq or Lean

sources.heading: 2.1 The Deductive Ontology (Proof-Objects)

nodes.name: Coherence Across Ontologies Is Not Free
nodes.statement: Maintaining semantic, logical and analytic coherence across the ontologies carries a computational and conceptual cost that any implementation must budget for explicitly.

costs.note: conceptual cost of keeping three notions of equality aligned

sources.heading: 2.5 A Unifying Object and Morphism Layer
sources.quote: Coherence is not free; maintaining it across ontologies has a computational and conceptual cost

nodes.name: Tools That Capture and Manipulate Pre-Formal Material
nodes.statement: The recent availability of tools that can converse with, capture and manipulate pre-formal material is what makes the fuzzy layer treatable as a first-class ontology.

affordances: tools that can converse with, capture, and manipulate pre-formal material
